propositions: The rebar-implement skill dispatches an implementation subagent in Phase 4d without specifying a model tier, causing it to inherit the orchestrator's expensive model.
The skill lacks guidance on which work is safe to delegate to cheaper models and how to escalate when a cheap implementer is insufficient.
A Model tiering section with a capability-tier table (strong/standard/cheap) should map both Claude Code and Codex CLI examples per tier without hardcoding product names.
Phase 4d should default to standard tier, restrict cheap tier to transcription-only leaves, and require constraints in the brief.
A 4e-bis escalation ladder should distinguish normal held-out iteration from model-weakness escalation triggers while preserving the held-out-TDD invariant.
The change is docs-only, touches only SKILL.md, cites .github/module-size-limit.txt as the module-size source of truth, and must pass make lint.
